entries.title: Isaiah 7:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Ahaz, being troubled with fear of Rezin and Pekah, is comforted by Isaiah. 10 Ahaz, having liberty to choose a sign, and refusing it, hath for a sign, Christ promised. 17 His judgment is prophesied to come by Assyria.

the days. 2Ki 16:1; 2Ch 28:1-6 Rezin. 8:6; 2Ki 15:37; Ps 83:3-5 but could. 4-9; 8:9,10

entries.title: Isaiah 7:3
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Go forth. Ex 7:15; Jer 19:2,3; 22:1 Shear-jashub. that is, The remnant shall return. 6:13; 10:21; 55:7; Ro 9:27 the end. 36:2; 2Ki 18:17; 20:20 highway. or, causeway.

entries.title: Isaiah 7:4
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Take heed. 30:7,15; Ex 14:13,14; 2Ch 20:17; La 3:26 fear not. 8:11-14; 35:4; 41:14; 51:12,13; Mt 10:28; 24:6 neither be faint-hearted. Heb. let not they heart be tender. De 20:3; 1Sa 17:32 the two tails. 8; 8:4; 2Ki 15:29,30; Am 4:11

entries.title: Isaiah 7:6
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: vex. or, waken. lit. disgust. .

entries.title: Isaiah 7:8
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
For the head.Dr. Jubb transposes the former part of ver. 9, and renders, "Though the head of Syria be Damascus; and the head of Damascus Retzin; and the head of Ephraim be Samaria; and the head of Samaria Remaliah's son; yet within threescore and five years Ephraim shall be broken, that he be no more a people." This renders the passage perfectly clear; and the prophecy received its full accomplishment when Esarhaddon carried away the remains of the ten tribes.

2Sa 8:6 within. 8:4; 17:1-3; 2Ki 17:5-23; Ezr 4:2 that it be not a people. Heb. from a people. Ho 1:6-10

entries.title: Isaiah 7:9
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: the head. 1Ki 16:24-29; 2Ki 15:27 If ye, etc. or, ye not believe? it is because ye are notstable. 2Ch 20:20; Ac 27:11,25; Ro 11:20; Heb 11:6; 1Jo 5:10

entries.title: Isaiah 7:10
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Moreover, etc. Heb. and the Lord added to speak. 1:5,13; 8:5; 10:20; Ho 13:2; *marg:

entries.title: Isaiah 7:11
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: a sign. 37:30; 38:7,8,22; Jud 6:36-40; 2Ki 20:8-11; Jer 19:1,10; 51:63,64 Mt 12:38-40; 16:1-4 ask it either in the depth. or, make thy petition deep.

entries.title: Isaiah 7:12
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: I will not ask. 2Ki 16:15; 2Ch 28:22 neither. Eze 33:31 tempt. De 6:16; Mal 3:15; Ac 5:9; 1Co 10:9

entries.title: Isaiah 7:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: Behold. Ge 3:15; Jer 31:22; Mt 1:23; Lu 1:35 shall call. or, thou, O virgin, shalt call. Ge 4:1,2,25; 16:11; 29:32; 30:6,8; 1Sa 1:20; 4:21 Immanuel. 8:8; 9:6; Joh 1:1,2,14; Ro 9:5; 1Ti 3:16

entries.title: Isaiah 7:15
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Butter.Connecting this verse with the preceding and following, we may render with Dr. Jubb and Lowth, "Behold the virgin ({h��lmah,} as the word uniformly signifies, Ge 24:43. Ex 2:8. Ps 68:26. Pr 30:19. So 1:3; 6:8.) shall conceive and bear a son, and thou shalt call his name Immanuel; butter and honey shall he eat when he shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good. For," etc.

22; Mt 3:4 know. Ps 51:5; Am 5:15; Lu 1:35; 2:40,52; Ro 12:9; Php 1:9,10

entries.title: Isaiah 7:19
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: in the holes. 2:19,21; 2Ch 33:11; Jer 16:16; Mic 7:17 bushes. or, commendable trees.

entries.title: Isaiah 7:22
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: butter and honey. 15; 2Sa 17:29; Mt 3:4 land. Heb. midst of the land.

entries.title: Isaiah 7:23
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: a thousand vines. So 8:11,12; Mt 21:33 be for briers. 5:6; 32:12-14; Jer 4:26; Heb 6:8
